# ZViewer

> ZViewer is an offline native Android comic reader for local archives (ZIP/CBZ, RAR/CBR, 7Z), PDF, image folders, and video folders, built with Kotlin 2.1 and Jetpack Compose (Material 3).

Package `dev.zolive.zviewer`, version 1.4.5 (`versionCode 15`), MIT license. Targets Android 10+ (minSdk 29, compile/target SDK 36); the universal APK covers `arm64-v8a` and `x86_64`. Everything runs on-device: the app requests no network or storage permissions and reads only a user-selected library folder through a persisted Storage Access Framework (SAF) grant. UI strings and the Chinese docs are in Simplified Chinese.

## Features

- Library: recursive scan, natural filename sorting (`2.jpg` before `10.jpg`), covers, search, reading-status filter, and Library / Favorites / Recently Read tabs that can be switched by swiping. Long-press a cover to enter favorite management, where tapping a cover or its button toggles the favorite. Search, filters, sorting, and tab switches keep management mode on. The close button, Settings, refresh, system back, or picking a new library folder exits it.
- Reader: continuous vertical scrolling or horizontal paging, optional right-to-left paging, loop mode (first and last pages adjoin), pinch / double-tap / button zoom from 1× to 5×, page jump, keep screen on, and saved per-page and per-video progress.
- Video: folders or archives that contain only videos, or a mix of images and videos, open in one pager that follows the vertical/horizontal setting. The seek slider appears only on video pages. Options: loop a single video, or open in preview mode (paused until tapped). Codec support depends on the device's Media3 / system decoders.
- Settings sections: Appearance (follow-system / light / dark theme, preset or custom accent color), Preferences (2–5 cover columns, show file type [off by default], show favorite icon [on by default]), Reading, Library & Storage (library folder, clear cache, clear reading history), and Diagnostics. Swipe right or use system back to leave Settings.
- Diagnostic log (optional): written to the app-specific external `logs/` directory by default, or to a SAF folder the user picks.
- Storage: the reading cache (extracted pages, copied images, PDF renders, covers, video frames) starts LRU reclamation at about 1.5 GiB and trims to about 1 GiB. Books that are open and files still being written are protected, so the limit is soft. Clearing the cache or reading history never touches original files or favorites.

## Supported Formats

| Kind | Extensions |
| --- | --- |
| Archives | `zip`, `cbz`, `rar`, `cbr`, `7z` (via libarchive) |
| Documents | `pdf` (via `PdfRenderer`; library root or plain subfolders only) |
| Static images | `jpg`, `jpeg`, `png`, `webp`, `bmp`, `heif`, `heic`, `avif` |
| Animated images | `apng`, animated `webp`, `gif`, animated `avif` (via APNG4Android + libavif) |
| Video | `mp4`, `m4v`, `mkv`, `webm`, `avi`, `mov`, `3gp`, `3g2`, `mpg`, `mpeg`, `ts`, `mts`, `m2ts`, `flv`, `wmv`, `ogv`, `vob`, `rm`, `rmvb` |

Not supported: encrypted or multi-volume archives, password-protected PDFs, PDFs inside archives (the user is asked to extract them first), DRM content, animated HEIF. HEIF/HEIC decoding depends on the device. A solid 7Z archive has to be fully prepared on first open.

## Architecture

Source root: `app/src/main/java/dev/zolive/zviewer/`.

- `MainActivity.kt`: the single Activity; edge-to-edge Compose host.
- `LibraryViewModel.kt`: app state, SAF folder selection, scan/open jobs, error mapping, settings, and progress.
- `data/Models.kt`: `Book`, `BookSession`, media-aware `PageSource`, `ReadingProgress`, `ReaderSettings`, `NaturalOrder`, `ReaderException`.
- `data/PreferenceStore.kt`: SharedPreferences storage for the tree URI, the book index JSON, page/video progress, favorites, settings, and log options.
- `data/BookRepository.kt`: bulk `DocumentsContract` queries, background extraction, PDF rendering, video preparation, cover and page caches, and safety limits.
- `data/ReadingCache.kt`: size accounting and LRU trimming of `books/` and `covers/`, with reference-counted protection for open books.
- `data/DiagnosticLog.kt`: an optional log, one file per process (`zviewer-<date>-<time>.log`), covering lifecycle, scan/open, video playback and surface events, the player pool, cover timing, and uncaught exceptions. Writes are serialized on an IO coroutine; the crash handler flushes synchronously. If the chosen folder can't be written, it falls back to the default directory.
- `reader/ImageLoader.kt`: APNG detection from PNG chunks, AVIF via APNG4Android + libavif, all other formats via `ImageDecoder`.
- `reader/SampledAnimationDrawable.kt`: draws animations at a downsampled target size.
- `reader/ZoomImageView.kt`, `reader/ZoomVideoView.kt`: native matrix zoom/pan inside an `AndroidView`. Unzoomed gestures pass through to the Compose list or pager. The video view keeps a cached first-frame cover behind the Media3 `TextureView`.
- `reader/ReaderPaging.kt`: maps virtual loop positions to real page numbers for `LazyColumn` / `HorizontalPager`.
- `ui/LibraryScreen.kt`: `ZViewerApp` entry point, library tabs and grid, search/filter, continue-reading card, favorite management.
- `ui/ReaderScreen.kt`: the image reader and its shared toolbar.
- `ui/VideoReader.kt`: Media3 playback. Details are below.
- `ui/SettingsScreen.kt`, `ui/Theme.kt`: Material 3 settings (with the swipe-right exit gesture) and theming.

Video playback design (`ui/VideoReader.kt`):

- Player pool: players are preloaded for the settled page and its two neighbours, at most three. Each off-screen neighbour renders its saved-position first frame into its own `TextureView`, so swiping never creates or destroys a surface. A player is released once its page is two or more positions away or leaves the composition, so aborted or back-and-forth drags reuse the same instance. Looping duplicate items never all get players. Pages farther out show only a cover from a session LRU cache.
- No flashing: every video page has the same `AndroidView` structure with or without a player. The Media3 shutter is transparent and the cover sits behind the video until the first frame paints over it. Each player belongs to exactly one view, and ownership moves by detaching the old view before binding the new one. Playback also requires the owning surface to be attached.
- `repeatMode` is set only from the loop settings and is never changed during transitions. Changing it near the end of a clip makes ExoPlayer reinitialize its output and flash. Instead, a video that ends mid-transition restarts from the beginning in `onEnded`, and a finished video restarts when the user returns to it.
- Video folders play directly from SAF URIs. Videos inside archives play from extracted files. Covers come from `MediaMetadataRetriever` using the first video in natural order.

Data flow: the user picks a folder → persisted SAF read grant → background recursive scan → book index → covers generated on demand → a book is opened → images decoded or archive members extracted → visible media shown or played → page / video index and video position saved.

## Privacy and Security

- No `INTERNET`, external-storage, or `MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` permission. No accounts, ads, or telemetry.
- Only the granted directory is read. Original files are never modified, moved, or deleted.
- Backup and device-to-device transfer are disabled, so URI grants don't move with app data.
- Archive members are written under generated sequential filenames. Hidden files, `__MACOSX`, symlinks, and unsupported entries are skipped. Member names are decoded as UTF-8 (`Archive.setCharset`) so Chinese names work.
- Safety limits: 20,000 pages per book, 256 MB per image, 4 GB extracted per book, archive scan depth 32.

## Build and Test

Requirements: JDK 17, Android SDK 36, the bundled Gradle 8.11.1 wrapper (AGP 8.10.1), and network access to download dependencies.

```sh
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-17-openjdk-amd64
export ANDROID_HOME="$HOME/Android"
./gradlew :app:assembleDebug :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:lintDebug
./gradlew :app:connectedDebugAndroidTest   # instrumented tests on an emulator/device
./gradlew :app:assembleRelease             # signed release build
```

- Unit tests (`app/src/test/`): `NaturalOrderTest` (ordering, hidden files, cache keys, extensions), `ReadingCacheTest` (limits, LRU order, protection of books in use), `ReaderPagingTest` (loop boundaries, single-page and large books).
- Instrumented tests (`app/src/androidTest/`): `FormatIntegrationTest` (every archive/PDF/image format, corrupt or empty archives, path traversal, large APNG), `VideoIntegrationTest`, `ReaderInteractionTest`, `NavigationInteractionTest` (tab swipes, Settings transitions and swipe exit), `FavoriteManagementTest`, `CacheIntegrationTest`, `DiagnosticLogTest`. SAF access is provided by `FixtureDocumentsProvider`.
- Fixtures: `tools/generate_fixtures.py` and `tools/generate_video_fixtures.py` (needs FFmpeg) write to `tools/fixtures/`, which is packaged as androidTest assets.
- Emulator UI smoke scripts (uiautomator2): `tools/ui_smoke.py`, `tools/ui_navigation_smoke.py`, `tools/ui_cache_smoke.py`. `tools/collect_licenses.py` regenerates the open source notices.
- Release signing: `.signing/zviewer-release.jks` (alias `zviewer`), with passwords from `ZVIEWER_STORE_PASSWORD` / `ZVIEWER_KEY_PASSWORD`. Never commit `.signing/`.
- Output: development builds go to `app/build/outputs/apk/release/`. Official release APKs and their SHA-256 checksums go to `dist/` (e.g. `ZViewer-1.4.5-release.apk`).

## Key Dependencies

Compose BOM `2025.05.01`, `activity-compose:1.10.1`, `lifecycle:2.9.0`, `core-ktx:1.16.0`, Media3 `exoplayer` / `ui` `1.6.1`, kotlinx-coroutines `1.10.2`, `me.zhanghai.android.libarchive:library:1.1.6`, APNG4Android `apng` / `avif` `3.0.5`, `org.aomedia.avif.android:avif:1.3.0.841110fd`.
